source_text: Μεταμόρφωσις ἀνθρώποις μεμυθολόγηται· μεταμορφοῦνται δὲ παρ᾿ ὑμῖν καὶ οἱ θεοί.Δένδρον ἡ Ῥέα γίνεται, δράκων δὲ ὁ Ζεὺς διὰ τὴν Φερσέφατταν, αἴγειροι αἱ τοῦ Φαέθοντος ἀδελφαί, καὶ ἡ Λητὼ ζῶον εὐτελές, δι᾿ ἣν Ὀρτυγία Δῆλος ἡ νῦν κέκληται. Θεὸς εἰπέ μοι κύκνος γίνεται, καὶ τὴν ἀετοῦ μορφὴν ἀναλαμβάνει, καὶ δι᾿ οἰνοχοΐαν τοῦ Γανυμήδους τῇ παιδεραστίᾳ σεμνύνεται; Τί μοι σέβειν θεοὺς δωρολήπτας, καὶ ὀργιζομένους ἂν μὴ λάβωσιν; Ἐχέτωσαν οὗτοι τὴν εἱμαρμένην· τοὺς πλανήτας προσκυνεῖν οὐ βούλομαι. Τίς ἐστιν ὁ Βερενίκης πλόκαμος; Ποῦ δὲ οἱ ἀστέρες αὐτῆς πρὶν τὴν προειρημένην ἀποθανεῖν; Πῶς δὲ ὁ τεθνεὼς Ἀντίνοος μειράκιον ἐν τῇ σελήνῃ ὡραῖον καθίδρυται; Τίς ὁ ἀναβιβάσας αὐτόν, εἰ μή τις καὶ τοῦτον, ὡς τοὺς βασιλέας μισθοῦ δι᾿ ἐπιορκίας τις, τοὺς θεοὺς καταγελῶν, εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν ἀνεληλυθέναι φήσας πεπίστευται, κατὰ τὸ ὅμοιον θεολογήσας τιμῆς καὶ δωρεᾶς ἠξίωται; Τί μοι τὸν θεον σεσυλήκατε; Τί δὲ αὐτοῦ τὴν ποίησιν ἀτιμάζετε; Θύεις πρόβατον, τὸ δ᾿ αὐτὸ προσκυνεῖς· ταῦρός ἐστιν ἐν οὐρανῷ, καὶ τὴν εἰκόνα σφάττεις αὐτοῦ. Ζῶον πονηρὸν ὁ ἐνγόνασι ἐκθλίβει· καὶ τὸν ἀνθρωποποιὸν Προμηθία καταφαγών ἀετὸς τετίμηται.Καλὸς ὁ κύκνος, ὅτι μοιχὸς ἦν· καλοὶ δὲ καὶ οἱ ἑτεροήμεροι Διόσκουροι, τῶν Λευκιππίδων οἱ ἁρπασταί. Κρείττων ἡ Ἑλένη, τὸν μὲν καρήξανθον Μενέλαον καταλιποῦσα, τῷ δὲ μιτρηφόρῳ καὶ πολυχρύσῳ Πάριδι κατακολουθοῦσα. Λίκαιος καὶ Σώφρων, ὁ τὴν ἐκπορνεύσασαν εἰς Ἠλύσια πεδία μετατεθεικώς. Ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ ἡ Τυνδαρὶς ἀπηθανάτισται· καὶ σοφῶς ὁ Εὐριπίδης ὑπὸ Ὀρέστου τῆς προειρημένης γυναικὸς τὴν ἀναίρεσιν παρεισήγαγε.
pass_a_gloss: Transformation is mythologized for humans; but also the gods are transformed among you. The Rea becomes a tree, and Zeus becomes a serpent through Persephatta, the poplars are the sisters of Phaethon, and Leto becomes a lowly animal, because of which Delos is now called Ortygia. Tell me, does God become a swan, and take on the form of an eagle, and is he honored because of the wine-pouring of Ganymede and his pederasty? Why should I reverence gods who are bribed and become angry if they do not receive? Let them have their fate; I do not wish to worship the planets. What is the lock of Berenice? And where are her stars before the aforementioned woman died? And how is the dead Antinous, a beautiful youth, established in the moon? Who has lifted him up, if not someone who, like the kings for a wage through perjury, mocking the gods, has said that he has gone up into heaven, and has been deemed worthy of honor and gift according to the same theology? Why have you plundered God? And why do you dishonor his creation? You sacrifice a sheep, and yet you worship the same thing; a bull is in heaven, and you slaughter its image. A wicked animal, the eagle, is revered because it tore out Prometheus' liver; and the one who created humans, Prometheus, is devoured by an eagle. The swan is beautiful because it was an adulterer; and the Dioscuri, the abductors of the Leucippides, are also beautiful. Helen is better, having left the grey-haired Menelaus and having followed the mitre-wearing and rich Paris. Lycaon and Socrates, who transferred the one who prostituted herself to the Elysian fields. But not even Tyndareus' daughter has been deified; and wisely Euripides introduced the destruction of the aforementioned woman by Orestes.

pass_b_english: Humans mythologize transformation, but among you the gods themselves undergo it. Rhea turns into a tree; Zeus becomes a serpent because of Persephone. The sisters of Phaethon become poplars, and Leto becomes a lowly creature — that is why the island once called Ortygia is now Delos. Are we to believe that God turns into a swan, assumes the form of an eagle, and is honored for Ganymede’s wine-pouring and his pederasty? Why should I revere gods who take bribes and grow angry when they do not receive them? Let them keep their fate; I refuse to worship the planets. What is the lock of Berenice? Where were her stars before that woman died? How is the dead Antinous, a beautiful youth, established in the moon? Who lifted him up, if not someone who — like kings who perjure themselves for a wage while mocking the gods — claimed he ascended to heaven and, by the same theology, was deemed worthy of honor and reward? Why have you plundered God? Why do you dishonor his creation? You sacrifice a sheep, yet you worship the very same thing; a bull is in heaven, and you slaughter its image. The eagle, a wicked animal, is revered because it tore out Prometheus’ liver; and Prometheus, the maker of humankind, is devoured by an eagle. The swan is beautiful because it was an adulterer; the Dioscuri, abductors of the Leucippides, are beautiful as well. Helen is better: she left grey-haired Menelaus and followed the mitre-wearing, gold-rich Paris. Lycaon and Socrates — the one who transferred the woman who prostituted herself to the Elysian fields. Yet even Tyndareus’ daughter has not been deified; and wisely Euripides introduced her destruction by Orestes.

review.notes: Pass A and Pass B both fail to correctly translate the clause regarding Leto and Delos. The Greek 'δι᾿ ἣν Ὀρτυγία Δῆλος ἡ νῦν κέκληται' indicates that Delos is the one now called Ortygia (or vice versa, depending on the reading of the relative pronoun, but the identity is between the two names). Pass A says 'Delos is now called Ortygia', while Pass B says 'the island once called Ortygia is now Delos'. However, the Greek 'δι᾿ ἣν' (through which/by which) refers to the 'lowly animal' (ζῶον εὐτελές) mentioned previously, implying the animal/event is the reason for the name change. More critically, Pass A and Pass B both fail on 'Λίκαιος καὶ Σώφρων'. The Greek text says 'Λίκαιος καὶ Σώφρων, ὁ τὴν ἐκπορνεύσασαν εἰς Ἠλύσια πεδία μετατεθεικώς'. Pass A translates 'Σώφρων' as 'Socrates', which is a significant error as 'Σώφρων' (Sophron) is a proper name, not 'Socrates' (Σωκράτης). Pass B also translates 'Σώφρων' as 'Socrates'. This is a hallucination/error in both translations. Additionally, Pass A translates 'ἐκθλίβει' as 'tears out' (in the context of the eagle/Prometheus) but the Greek 'ἐκθλίβει' (to crush/press out) is used for the 'wicked animal' (the eagle) in the sentence 'Ζῶον πονηρὸν ὁ ἐνγόνασι ἐκθλίβει', which refers to the eagle crushing the entrails, whereas the Prometheus clause is separate. The translation of 'Σώφρων' as 'Socrates' is a definitive failure of fidelity.
reasons: Pass A and Pass B both translate 'Σώφρων' as 'Socrates', which is incorrect; the Greek is the proper name 'Sophron'.
Pass A and Pass B fail to accurately render the causal relationship in the Leto/Delos clause regarding the 'lowly animal'.
